title: Bram and the Protocol Again
premise: Mara Dunmore has spent nine years alone tending Earth's last seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony fleet that stopped answering long ago. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream — a garden growing inside a metal heart — Mara discovers the dreams are a message routed through her vault's dormant AI, Bram, from a faction hiding aboard the fleet. The message can expose the war crimes that started the fleet's civil conflict and force a peace before the truce expires, but delivering it means choosing between the duty she swore to the dead Earth and the love she never expected to feel for Ilya, the dreamer sent to silence her. In the end, Mara broadcasts the truth to both fleets at once, ending the war but exiling herself — until the children's dream shows her a new world where the seeds, and she, finally belong.
about_author: Ulyana Almeida is a former agricultural engineer who spent a decade working in remote research stations before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep things alive when no one is watching.

chapters.title: The Last Gardener
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Establishes her solitary routine inside the seed vault: cataloging, rationing power, recording logs no one answers. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as competence, and the first flicker of doubt that anyone is listening.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Mara detects an anomalous transmission buried in static — not from Earth, but from the colony fleet's direction. She debates whether to respond. Emotional beat: hope arriving as something frightening.

chapters.title: Bram Wakes
chapters.summary: The vault's ancient AI, Bram, boots up unprompted after years of dormancy, claiming it received instructions it cannot disclose. Mara realizes someone out there still knows the vault exists. Emotional beat: unease beneath wonder.

chapters.title: Children of the Fleet
chapters.summary: POV shift to Sefa, a twelve-year-old aboard the colony ship Meridian, who wakes screaming from a shared dream of a garden inside a machine. Her mother silences her; such talk is dangerous during the truce. Emotional beat: fear of being different.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Fleet POV through Commander Oyelaran: the civil war's ceasefire expires in forty days, and hardliners on both sides want the war finished. A directive goes out to find the source of the 'dream contagion.' Emotional beat: dread of inevitability.

chapters.title: What Bram Knows
chapters.summary: Bram admits fragments: the dreams are a compressed message, split among sleeping minds because direct transmission would be intercepted. The key to assembling it lies in the vault itself. Emotional beat: Mara's anger at being made a pawn.

chapters.title: Ilya Descends
chapters.summary: A shuttle breaches atmosphere against orders — Ilya Voss, a fleet linguist and secret member of the message-faction, arrives at the vault to retrieve or destroy the message, he isn't sure which. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other instantly.

chapters.title: Negotiating with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Mara and Ilya circle each other over weeks of forced cooperation while Bram stalls them both. Flashbacks reveal Ilya lost his sister to the war's first atrocity. Emotional beat: guarded intimacy.

chapters.title: Sefa's Map
chapters.summary: Sefa POV. The dreaming children begin drawing the same impossible map — of the vault's interior, a place none have seen. Fleet security notices. Emotional beat: the children realize they are instruments, and choose curiosity over fear.

chapters.title: The Hardliner's Visit
chapters.summary: Commander Oyelaran's enforcer, Dain Reeve, traces the signal to Earth and demands Ilya hand over the vault. Ilya lies; Mara watches him do it and understands his allegiance. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into commitment.

chapters.title: Seeds as Keys
chapters.summary: Bram reveals the message is encoded in the vault's own archive — each seed lot a cipher fragment planted by the fleet's founders before the war. Assembling it requires opening sealed sections Mara swore never to touch. Emotional beat: duty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The First Seal
chapters.summary: Mara opens the founders' wing and finds evidence the war began over this vault: Earth's biological legacy was the prize both factions fought to control. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal — her sacred duty was always political.

chapters.title: Dreaming Together
chapters.summary: Through Bram's relay, Mara enters the children's shared dream and meets Sefa mind-to-mind. The dream shows the assembled message: proof of who committed the founding atrocity. Emotional beat: belonging so intense it hurts.

chapters.title: Love Against Orders
chapters.summary: Ilya confesses his faction ordered him to kill Mara once the message was secured. He refuses. They become lovers knowing the fleet will come for both. Emotional beat: tenderness under a countdown.

chapters.title: Reeve Returns
chapters.summary: Dain Reeve storms the vault with marines, takes Bram offline, and arrests Ilya. Mara hides in the deep archive with the final cipher fragment. Emotional beat: everything she built torn open.

chapters.title: The Children Refuse
chapters.summary: Sefa POV. The dreaming children, interrogated by fleet security, synchronize deliberately and overwhelm the ship's systems with the dream, buying Mara time. Emotional beat: the powerless discovering collective power.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Alone, Mara completes the message using the seed ciphers and her own maintenance logs — nine years of witnessing what everyone forgot becomes part of the testimony. Emotional beat: her invisibility transfigured into authority.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Mara reactivates Bram, frees Ilya mid-transit, and broadcasts the full message — atrocity evidence plus her logs — simultaneously to both fleets before the truce expires. Reeve tries to jam it; the children hold the channel open from their end. Emotional beat: terrible courage.

chapters.title: The War That Didn't Start
chapters.summary: Fleet POV. The truth shatters both factions' narratives; mutinies on both sides force commanders to accept arbitration instead of resuming war. Oyelaran chooses peace over pride. Emotional beat: exhausted relief, disbelief.

chapters.title: Tribunal and Cost
chapters.summary: Reeve faces judgment; Ilya is pardoned but marked a traitor by half the fleet. Mara learns the price of the broadcast: the vault's power core is failing, and Earth's seeds will die without a new home. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: The Garden in the Dream
chapters.summary: The children's dream resolves into coordinates — a habitable moon the founders had hidden in the archive all along. The fleet votes to land there and carry the vault's seeds with them. Emotional beat: hope earned, not given.

chapters.title: Where Belonging Grows
chapters.summary: Resolution. On the new world, Mara plants the first seeds as the children — Sefa foremost — work beside her, and Ilya stands at her shoulder. Bram, relocated, records its first log of growth instead of decay. Emotional beat: homecoming, and the quiet end of exile.
